rules.label: Colorado Financial Assistance 0-250% FPL
rules.quote: The legislation requires hospitals to provide financial assistance to patients in emergent situations and whose incomes are less than 250 percent of the current year’s federal poverty level.

payment_plan.quote: is committed to offering reasonable payment plan options to its patients, and will allow for at least 30 days past the payment due date before pursuing collections.

notes: The policy mentions treatment of emergent and urgent patients regardless of ability to pay or coverage status, but this is not a formal requirement for financial assistance eligibility.

The policy references compliance with PPACA, IRC Section 501(r), and Colorado Senate Bill 14-50, but these are not modeled as specific eligibility criteria beyond the 250% FPL requirement for Colorado Financial Assistance.
Copayment minimums are noted with asterisks but not modeled as they relate to patient cost-sharing rather than discount percentage.
The policy includes Kansas and Utah facilities with different FPL brackets, modeled as separate rules.
The policy mentions screening uninsured patients for financial assistance when possible, but this is procedural and not a requirement for assistance.
co_fap_0_250 may leave out a condition: policy limits assistance to emergent situations only, not all medically necessary care
